questions.q: Which of the three main states of matter has a fixed shape and a fixed volume?
a: Solid
Liquid
Gas
Plasma

questions.q: How are particles arranged in a typical solid according to the particle model?
a: Randomly arranged and moving very fast in all directions
Tightly packed together in a regular, fixed lattice pattern vibrating in place
Spread far apart with almost no forces between them
Clustered in small floating groups that slide past each other

questions.q: Which state of matter takes the shape of its container, has a fixed volume, and its particles can flow or slide past one another?
a: Solid
Gas
Liquid
Rigid crystal

questions.q: What happens to the movement and arrangement of particles when a liquid turns into a gas during boiling?
a: Particles become closer together and form a regular crystal lattice
Particles slow down and stop moving completely
Particles arrange themselves into rigid rows
Particles gain enough energy to break free from each other, moving rapidly in all directions

questions.q: What is the term for the phase change when a substance changes directly from a solid to a gas without becoming a liquid first?
a: Sublimation
Melting
Condensation
Evaporation

questions.q: Why can gases be easily compressed (squashed) into a smaller volume?
a: Because gas particles are tightly locked in place
Because there are large empty spaces between the widely separated gas particles
Because gas particles shrink in size when pressure is applied
Because gas particles turn into liquids under pressure

questions.q: What is the name of the physical process where a liquid changes into a gas at temperatures below its boiling point?
a: Freezing
Melting
Evaporation
Sublimation

questions.q: According to the particle model of matter, what are all substances made of?
a: Continuous, unbroken sheets of jelly
Invisible magnetic fields
Fluid energy waves
Tiny moving particles (atoms, molecules, or ions)

questions.q: What term describes the change of state from a gas to a liquid when it cools down?
a: Condensation
Melting
Boiling
Sublimation

questions.q: During the melting of pure ice into water, what happens to the temperature of the substance while the change of state is taking place?
a: The temperature increases rapidly
The temperature stays constant at 0 degrees Celsius until all the ice has melted
The temperature drops below zero
The temperature fluctuates up and down

questions.q: Which property best explains why a liquid can flow and pour easily?
a: Its particles are bonded in rigid positions
Its particles have zero kinetic energy
Its particles are close together but free to slide past one another
Its particles repel each other into outer space

questions.q: What happens to the average speed and kinetic energy of particles when a substance is heated?
a: They slow down and pack closer together
They turn into solid crystals
They stop moving entirely
They gain kinetic energy and move faster

questions.q: What is diffusion defined as in terms of the particle model?
a: The net random movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration
The forced pumping of liquid through a narrow pipe
The chemical reaction between a solid and a gas
The freezing of particles into a solid block

questions.q: Why does diffusion happen much faster in gases than in liquids?
a: Gas particles are heavier than liquid particles
Gas particles move much faster and have greater space between them than liquid particles
Liquids have stronger forces holding particles together than gases
Gases are always kept at higher temperatures than liquids

questions.q: What change of state occurs when liquid water turns into solid ice in a freezer?
a: Melting
Evaporation
Freezing (Solidification)
Condensation

questions.q: When a solid melts into a liquid, what happens to the forces of attraction between the particles?
a: The forces become much stronger, locking particles tighter
The forces remain completely unchanged
The forces disappear entirely
The forces weaken sufficiently to allow particles to move past each other rather than stay in fixed positions

questions.q: Which of the following substances sublimes at standard atmospheric pressure (turns directly from solid to gas)?
a: Solid carbon dioxide (dry ice) or iodine
Liquid mercury
Iron metal
Pure water ice

questions.q: Why do balloon walls stay inflated under gas pressure from the inside?
a: Because the rubber material attracts external air
Because moving gas particles inside constantly collide with the inner walls of the balloon
Because the gas particles inside freeze against the rubber
Because gravity pulls the gas downward

questions.q: What physical feature distinguishes boiling from evaporation?
a: Boiling happens only at room temperature
Evaporation only happens in closed metal containers
Boiling occurs at a specific fixed temperature throughout the entire liquid, whereas evaporation happens at any temperature only at the liquid surface
Boiling requires no thermal energy input

questions.q: If you open a bottle of perfume in the corner of a classroom, students across the room eventually smell it. Which scientific process explains this?
a: Thermal conduction
Magnetic attraction
Gravity filtration
Diffusion of gas particles

questions.q: In which state of matter are the forces of attraction between particles strongest?
a: Solid
Liquid
Gas
Plasma

questions.q: What happens to the volume of most substances when they are heated (thermal expansion)?
a: Their volume decreases because particles shrink
Their volume increases because particles vibrate more vigorously and push slightly further apart
Their volume stays completely constant
Their particles turn into gas instantly

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the particles in a gas?
a: They are arranged in neat rows and columns
They vibrate only about fixed positions
They are widely spaced, move randomly at high speeds, and fill any available container
They are tightly packed and cannot move

questions.q: When steam condenses on a cold bathroom window, what is happening to the energy of the water particles?
a: They absorb more heat energy from the glass
They increase their speed and move further apart
They turn into solid ice crystals instantly
They lose thermal energy to the surroundings, slow down, and form liquid droplets

questions.q: Why are liquids described as being virtually incompressible?
a: Because their particles are already packed closely together with very little empty space between them
Because liquid particles are made of solid rock
Because liquid particles repel each other strongly
Because liquids have no mass

questions.q: What causes gas pressure inside a sealed container?
a: Chemical reactions between the container walls and air
Collisions of fast-moving gas particles with the inner walls of the container
The weight of the container pressing down
Magnetic forces pulling the container inward

questions.q: Which of the following represents a physical change rather than a chemical change?
a: Burning wood in a fireplace
Cooking an egg
Ice melting into water
Iron rusting in damp air

questions.q: If you heat a metal rail on a railway track, what happens to the metal particles on a microscopic scale?
a: They melt into a puddle immediately
They disappear into the air
They break apart into individual atoms of different elements
They vibrate faster and take up slightly more average space, causing the rail to expand

questions.q: During a change of state from liquid to solid (freezing), what happens to the internal arrangement of particles?
a: Particles transition from a random arrangement to a regular, fixed lattice structure
Particles spread out to fill maximum space
Particles begin moving faster than before
Particles lose all mass

questions.q: Why does a puddle of water on a playground pavement dry up faster on a hot, windy day than on a cold, calm day?
a: Wind and heat cause water molecules to freeze
Higher temperature and air movement give particles more energy to evaporate quickly from the surface
The pavement absorbs the water molecules completely
Gravity pulls the water down through the concrete

questions.q: Which of the following lists the three states of matter in order of *increasing* particle spacing (from closest to furthest apart)?
a: Gas, Liquid, Solid
Liquid, Gas, Solid
Solid, Liquid, Gas
Gas, Solid, Liquid

questions.q: How does increasing the temperature of a gas inside a rigid, sealed container affect its pressure?
a: Pressure decreases because particles slow down
Pressure drops to zero
Pressure remains completely unaffected
Pressure increases because particles move faster and hit the container walls harder and more frequently
